_comment: The kinds of part on a shop's shelves (see docs/modding.md, "part_groups.json"). A part is in the first group with
a class its own class counts as (part_classes.json: "brake" takes in a disc_brake), the groups in
the order listed; a part no group takes in is an accessory. A mod's part_groups.json adds groups (tried before these)
or changes one of these by its id, naming only what it changes. The player reads part_group.<id> in the text, else
the group's name. never_stacks: never mounts on its own kind (a head on a head); bolt_on: what the cars on the lots
were worked on with; tune: how much a rival's tuner goes for it (10 the most, none: not at all); speed_shop: a speed
shop sells it; for_sale: parts of the kind are for sale at all (the paper, the mail order, the shelves; the running gear
is sold by what it is, a kind without it only as far as an engine build uses it: the mufflers, which only dress the
tailpipe, are not). The ids engine_blocks to shocks below
are the game's own: the engine's internals wear and break, the
running gear has a slot on each wheel. price: what a part of the kind costs new, in the game's dollars: base, and per_hp for
every horsepower the part is worth on the dyno (a block its engine's power, any other part what it makes over the
poorest of its kind in its place), the horsepower raised to hp_power first (none: 1); by a figure of its own (grip, brake_torque, rim_size, spring_rate, damping, carb_mounts) it
costs as much more or less as its figure stands against the middle one of its kind, to the power by_power (carb_mounts:
the carburettors a manifold takes: a kit no dyno run of the manifold alone measures). The
accessories group takes no classes: it prices the parts no group takes in.
shows: the parts view's buttons that put kinds of part out of sight. Each names its
groups (the first that names a part's group takes it); rest_of_engine takes every other part of the engine; a part
no show takes stays in sight. The player reads part_show.<id> as the button's tooltip. A mod adds shows, or changes
one by its id. The drivetrain is the gearbox (the flywheel and clutch are the engine's) and the rear axle with its
carrier, gears and shafts; a transfer case group a mod adds goes in it too. rear_axles to axle_shafts are the game's own
too: the rear axle has a slot on the car and takes the final drive and the differential over from the gearbox.
strength prices a kind by what it holds (Nm at the axle), diff_lock by how hard it locks. sway_bars and traction_bars
are the game's own as well: a sway bar has a slot across each axle (arb_rate prices it by its stiffness; the stock
ones, with none, stay off the shelves), a traction bar or a lowering block goes on a leaf spring. backing_plates and hubs too:
a backing plate goes on a corner's brake slot and carries a drum brake, a hub goes on a front drum or disc. brake_valves and
steering_kits too: a car slot each (the brake valve's in the lines, the angle kit's on the steering), empty from the
factory; what goes on them works by its adjust (brake_bias, steer_lock), and one that adjusts nothing is not sold.
